static_traits.name: Li Yiming
static_traits.family_status: Living alone; no further family details provided
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to confide in, but feels uncomfortable talking about poetry-related self-doubt, and there are concerns about others' evaluations in the relationships
static_traits.medical_history: No previous experience of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no notable physical disease
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic, high cooperation and a positive attitude; able to self-reflect and identify negative automatic thoughts; relatively sensitive to being judged; speech rate and specific expression style not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: After submitting poems to a competition and receiving no feedback, I concluded the judges disliked my work and were unwilling to comment, triggering and worsening self-doubt and worthlessness, persistently affecting my creativity and overall physical and mental state.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because self-doubt and negative thoughts are affecting my creativity and overall well-being, and I want to address these problems.

core_beliefs: My work is not worth appreciating / I have no value

special_situations.event: Three months after submitting a poem to a competition, still no feedback received
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no feedback is received, it means the work is terrible / they hate my poems
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking approval from friends to relieve self-doubt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They hate my work and do not want to bother giving feedback.

special_situations.event: Thinking about writing poetry again or joining future competitions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is not good enough, people will not appreciate it and I should not continue creating
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Temporarily avoids negative thoughts by distracting attention, and hesitates or even avoids submitting work and creating
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What is the point? The work will just be bad; no one will care.

special_situations.event: When talking with friends about self-doubt regarding poetry
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express vulnerability and unease, I will be judged or looked down on by friends
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing talk with friends about related topics; avoiding situations where one might be evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think my work is terrible and will judge me.

special_situations.event: Before a band performance, believing preparation is insufficient
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If preparation is insufficient, the performance will surely be a disaster
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Before a performance, repeatedly worries and negates oneself in an attempt to gain control

core_conflict.wish: Longing for one's work to be appreciated and recognized, and to be taken seriously
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being judged and negated, and thus feeling worthless
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of safety by avoiding exposure (reducing submissions and talking)
Short-term relief of unease and self-doubt by seeking external approval

object_relations.self_representation: A creator who is not good enough, a person easily negated
object_relations.object_representation: Reviewers/others are indifferent or harsh judges

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable person in front of friends
object_relations.object_representation: Friends may judge or look down on oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to examine evidence, propose alternative explanations, or suggests conducting reality testing (such as following up on submissions or proactively seeking feedback)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understands exploration as others possibly judging the work, worrying about being negated (transference: regarding others as potential judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle, supportive tone to first affirm their feelings; avoid directly negating their worries; use open-ended questions to guide them to distinguish facts from speculation, and encourage them to conduct reality testing in small steps.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about publicly displaying works or expressing self-doubt and unease to friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes exposing vulnerability will lead to rejection or mockery by others (transference: others as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Invite the client, in an empathic tone, to label the present experience with concrete emotion words; provide optional lightweight expressions (such as 'would you be willing to say a little about what you are worried about right now?'), allow pauses and silence, and gradually increase emotional tolerance.

manifestations: Difficulty opening up to friends, afraid of being judged
Feeling distanced from others in creative work (believing no one appreciates it)
Creative choices are constrained by external evaluation, relying on competitions and others' feedback to confirm worth
When facing writing and submitting, finds it hard to autonomously choose to keep trying

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing self-denial to 'they hate my poems' and 'unwilling to comment'
When mentioning friends or reviewers, presets that the other party holds negative views

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-doubt; believing the work is not good enough and does not deserve to be submitted
When talking with friends, excessively worrying about others' opinions and curtailing expression

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Avoiding directly facing self-doubt and unease by distracting attention
Changes the topic or reduces touching on sensitive creative-related content

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats competition feedback (or lack of feedback) as the absolute standard for evaluating the work's value
Internalizing outside evaluations unprocessed as judgments of self-worth

exception_events.target_problem: Before performances, the client usually predicts the worst outcome because of feeling underprepared, leading to marked self-doubt and tension, which in turn affects on-stage performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, a performance thought to be underprepared turned out to be one of the band's best performances, with the actual effect markedly better than the negative prediction.
exception_events.reason: Clues: although the client felt underprepared beforehand, the actual result contradicted the negative prediction, suggesting that their catastrophizing thinking is not inevitable; this experience provides them with a counterexample to draw on and a source of confidence.

positive_force: Has experience of performing well under negative expectations (a band performance that turned out unexpectedly well)
Has some social support (a few friends to confide in)
Positive attitude, willing to identify and challenge negative thinking
Able to propose reasonable alternative explanations (such as reviewers being busy, large submission volume)
negative_force: Seeking external validation, with sense of worth depending on others' feedback
Cognitive biases of catastrophizing prediction, jumping to conclusions, and mind reading
Highly sensitive to being judged; tends to avoid submitting work and talking about it
Excessive rumination leads to sleep disturbance, further weakening emotion regulation

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing predictions about and avoidance of creating and submitting work
antecedent: Thinking of their own poems or future competitions
Recalling experiences of not yet receiving feedback
Discussing work and self-doubt with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Interprets lack of feedback as the work being bad, with value depending on others' evaluations, producing cognitive biases of mind reading and fortune telling
target_behavior.function: Escaping the possibility of being judged and failing, temporarily lowering anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Creative and professional performance is impaired (band performance declines), sense of self-worth decreases, and sleep is disturbed

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently seeking external approval to counter unease
antecedent: Anxiety when thinking of competitions or writing
target_behavior.core_reason: Conditional assumption: only obtaining others' recognition proves I have worth
target_behavior.function: Obtaining comfort and a short-term sense of security
target_behavior.consequence: Dependence on others' evaluations intensifies, making it hard to establish internal standards, and negative thinking is not fundamentally changed
